solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A number of people run television for a county

parts.note: some people means a number of them, giving SOME
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a television is a TV set

explanation.surface: Some viewers race through television programmes about a particular English county.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is one of the shire counties of England, so it is an example of a county.

clue.text: Doctor has son to encourage

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A doctor's boy is there to cheer him along.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon is a medical practitioner who operates, so a kind of doctor.

clue.text: Mother queuing up to take drugs

parts.note: Ma is an informal word for mother
people queuing are standing in line

explanation.surface: Mum lining up to get her medication.
explanation.definitionFit: To mainline is slang for injecting drugs straight into a vein.

clue.text: Revolutionary is outside rabble-rousing?

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the radical stirring up crowds out in the street?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal on IS OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech incites people against authority, which is what rabble-rousing does.

clue.text: One hundred to an indefinite number

parts.note: in maths N stands for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A hundred going on to some unknown figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is informal British slang for a hundred, such as a hundred runs or a hundred pounds.

clue.text: Cut good tree

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to fell a fine tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a deep wound or slash, so it is a noun synonym for a cut.

clue.text: Idiot turned up with what may be Oxford detective

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool
an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe

explanation.surface: A fool appears beside an Inspector Morse-style detective from Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the city's detectives, but it is a type of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Gumshoe is American slang for a private detective.

clue.text: Bag carried by fans at Chelsea

indicators.note: carried by means held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bag held by football supporters at Chelsea.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, often used by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Barrier keeping tons off path

indicators.note: keeping, read with off later in the clue, means holding those letters away from the word
off completes keeping … off: the letters for tons are removed from the path word

parts.note: a trail is a path through countryside

explanation.surface: A fence that stops heavy vehicles from using a footpath.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail is a bar forming a fence or guard, so it is a kind of barrier.

clue.text: Explosive is key anytime, unfortunately

parts.note: D is a musical key

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of this word are muddled

explanation.surface: A warning that a crucial ingredient is volatile whenever it is handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' shuffles ANYTIME into YNAMITE, which follows D.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamite is a blasting compound based on nitroglycerine, an explosive substance.

clue.text: Wide-ranging elite, 300 in Rome are upset

indicators.note: letters that are upset are knocked out of order, so the pool is rearranged

parts.note: in Roman numerals C is 100, so 300 is CCC

explanation.surface: A broad-minded elite of three hundred people in Rome is unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic tastes draw on many different sources, which is what wide-ranging describes.

clue.text: Never-ending scales, see, when playing

indicators.note: letters at play are moved about freely, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A music teacher sighing over endless practice of scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceaseless means without stopping, so it is a synonym for never-ending.

clue.text: Unit working with energy

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A device that is running and drawing power.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the single whole number, the unit from which counting starts.

clue.text: Name talkative bird in short comment

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, inside it

parts.note: a note is a brief written comment
the mina (or myna) is a bird known for mimicking speech

explanation.surface: Naming a chatty bird in a brief remark.
explanation.walkthrough: Mina is a variant spelling of myna.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone for a role or award is to nominate them.

clue.text: Union rioting about cold papal emissary

indicators.note: one piece going about another wraps round it
rioting suggests disorder, so the letters of Union are thrown about

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A trade union protest breaks out around a chilly envoy from the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' turns UNION into NUNIO, and 'about' puts it round C.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is the Pope's diplomatic representative to a country, his ambassador.

clue.text: Pointless to exploit fewer

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it
less is a looser word for fewer

explanation.surface: There is no point exploiting a smaller number.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless serves no purpose, so it is pointless.

clue.text: Upset with what one needs to know when buying headgear

definitions.meaning: to upset a boat is to overturn it

definitions.text: what one needs to know when buying headgear

explanation.surface: Annoyed about the information needed when choosing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Capsize means overturn, and split as CAP SIZE it is a hat's fitting measurement.

clue.text: Ancient European in for a top Olympic medal

indicators.note: one piece sits in another, inside it

parts.note: gold is the medal for first place

explanation.surface: An elderly European contends for an Olympic gold medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has existed for a very long time, so it is ancient.

clue.text: Stray remark that's critical over topless robe

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another comes above it, so first

parts.note: a dig is a cutting remark

indicators.note: topless means the top, or first, letter is removed

parts.note: a robe is a long dress

explanation.surface: A disapproving comment about a revealing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops D from DRESS, leaving RESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject when speaking or writing.

clue.text: Marine mammal mostly seen here

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a seal is a mammal of the oceans and coasts, four letters long

explanation.surface: A note on where seals are usually spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: seals are mostly seen at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seals spend most of their lives in the ocean, so the sea is where they are mostly found.

clue.text: Forking out pence in mailing?

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, within it

parts.note: mailing a letter is sending it

explanation.surface: Wondering whether paying out means coins in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Forking out is an informal phrase for paying money, that is, spending.

clue.text: Be undersized and run down

parts.note: something undersized is little

explanation.surface: Being small and feeling exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to disparage them, which is to belittle them.

clue.text: Volunteers beginning of Bungalow Bill

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve army

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Volunteers start on the Beatles song 'Bungalow Bill'.
explanation.walkthrough: The Continuing Story of Bungalow Bill is a Beatles song.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab at a bar or restaurant.

clue.text: Call for a young man in uniform

definitions.meaning: to ... someone is to summon them over a loudspeaker or ...
a boy employed in livery at a hotel or court

explanation.surface: Sending for a youthful soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Page is both the verb for summoning someone and a uniformed boy attendant.

clue.text: Man, say, is left with ecstasy

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left; the answer also lies in 'is left' by coincidence, but the setter built it from IS, L and E
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man abandoned and left high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person, but it is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, which an isle is.

clue.text: Concern with bus in Essex dropping last two off

indicators.note: dropping off the last two letters of the word leaves only its first three

explanation.surface: Worry about a bus service in Essex losing its final two stops.
explanation.walkthrough: ESSEX is a county east of London; 'dropping last two off' leaves ESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern is a firm or company, which is a business.
